subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should OpenClaw support persistent browser Control UI device identity after the page is delivered over non-localhost plain HTTP?
rationale: The remaining change is not a current-code bug: docs and tests intentionally reject remote plaintext browser sessions without device identity, and changing that would redefine the Control UI authentication and tamper-resistance boundary.

options.title: Keep Secure-Context Boundary
options.body: Leave remote plain-HTTP device identity rejected and pursue warning/docs or trusted-proxy/Tailscale improvements for self-hosted users.

options.title: Add Explicit Opt-In Plaintext Identity
options.body: Support this homelab path only behind a named dangerous config/audit surface with tests and upgrade documentation.

options.title: Allow Pure-JS Identity Unconditionally
options.body: Remove the secure-context guard for all browser Control UI sessions, accepting the broader security-boundary change.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure-Context Boundary
recommendation.body: Leave remote plain-HTTP device identity rejected and pursue warning/docs or trusted-proxy/Tailscale improvements for self-hosted users.
